problems.field: studies[S1].design_class; studies[S1].assignment.randomized; reconciliation.agreed_fields_checked[0] (design_class = field_rct, randomized = yes)
problems.form_value: design_class 'field_rct' and randomized 'yes' with unit 'class', on the p. 5 sentence that the random assignment 'was conducted at the class level'. The agreed-fields entry marks this confirmed and cites p. 5 and p. 1, Abstract. The same form codes criterion_1 'unclear' and context_class 'observational'.
problems.source_says: The only claim of randomness is in Section 3.1, third paragraph: participants 'were randomly assigned to one of two groups', and the random assignment 'was conducted at the class level'. No page gives the number of classes or a randomization procedure. The paper calls its design quasi-experimental twice: in the abstract, and in the first paragraph of Section 3.1, which says the design was chosen over strict randomisation. The abstract, which the agreed-fields entry cites, says only 'assigned' and never 'random'. The form spec puts intact-class comparisons in quasi_people. With one class per arm, condition and class coincide and the design is quasi_people. Only with several classes per arm is it a cluster-randomized field_rct. The document does not say which, so field_rct (a core design code) is not supported, and it conflicts with the form's own criterion_1 'unclear' and context_class 'observational'. randomized 'yes' copies p. 5, but p. 5 places the randomization at the class level, not at the level of people. The analyses also treat the 74 students as independent (Levene's F(1, 72); Table 5 df2 = 69) and make no adjustment for class-level assignment.
problems.quote: The study adopted a quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test design. This design was chosen because it balances the rigour of experimental control with the ecological validity required in music classrooms, where strict randomisation and artificial manipulations risk disrupting pedagogical routines.
problems.locator: p. 5, Section 3.1, first paragraph (quasi-experimental design) and third paragraph (random assignment at the class level); p. 1, Abstract; p. 9, Results RQ2 (Levene's tests); p. 12, Table 5; form-spec.md, field note on design_class

confirmed.statement: The document states random assignment: 'In the present study, participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups.' The form's quote about class-level assignment is verbatim, and the PDF reads 'an unavoidable constraint'. unit 'class' is right.

No page states the number of classes, a randomization method, or a preregistration. A search of the text layer of all 19 pages (random, class, section, intact, cluster, allocat, regist, OSF) finds none of these. The only protocol statement is IRB approval, so preregistered 'not_stated' is right.
confirmed.locator: whole PDF (19 pages); p. 5, Section 3.1, last paragraph

confirmed.statement: What was assigned is access to ChatGPT-4 for the student's own coursework. 'The experimental group (n= 36) integrated ChatGPT-4 into their learning processes for tasks involving composition, improvisation, and music analysis', and the two environments 'were structured to differ only in the presence or absence of ChatGPT-4'. Students submitted their own creative product every two weeks, and blinded external assessors rated it. The arms do not differ only in whose output is evaluated.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Sections 3.1 and 3.2; p. 7, Sections 3.5 and 3.6

confirmed.statement: The tool is generative AI: ChatGPT-4, which the paper also calls 'the newer generation of ChatGPT-4 (i.e., ChatGPT-4o)'. Experimental-group students shared screenshots or links of their ChatGPT interactions.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 3.1, second paragraph; p. 7, Section 3.6

confirmed.statement: The comparison arm matches the form. The control group (n = 38) 'received instruction through traditional teacher-led methods without AI augmentation', used textbooks, class notes, and teacher consultation, and got feedback 'solely by the instructor without AI mediation'. The same instructor taught both groups. ai 'none' and comparison_type 'ai_vs_bau' fit.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Sections 3.1 and 3.2; p. 6, Table 1 and the text below it; p. 7, Section 3.6

confirmed.statement: The design is between-subjects. Each student was in one of the two groups for all 24 weeks, so check (e) on randomized order does not apply. structure 'between' is right.

Arm counts match. The paper gives n = 36 and n = 38 in the assignment sentence, and Table 6 lists N = 36 and N = 38. No exclusions are reported. Of 86 students in the programme, 12 did only the pilot.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 3.1; p. 12, Table 6; p. 7, Section 3.4

confirmed.statement: The form's doubts about balance hold. The paper says baseline tests 'confirmed comparability across the groups (see Tables 1 and 2)', but Table 1 summarizes the instruction and Table 2 reports growth-model fit. No baseline test is printed. The abstract says the experimental group 'began with higher initial levels', and Table 3 gives creativity intercepts of 3.281 (0.043) vs 3.004 (0.064).
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 3.1, third paragraph; p. 6, Tables 1 and 2; p. 1, Abstract; p. 9, Table 3

confirmed.statement: The participants come from the cohort of Zhou and Kim (2024), which the introduction describes as having '74 undergraduate music students in Korea'. The paper does not say whether students kept their earlier condition, and prior ChatGPT use enters only as a covariate. The form's open question on this is accurate.
confirmed.locator: p. 2, Introduction; p. 5, Section 3.1, second paragraph; p. 8, Section 3.7

summary: The PDF supports the form on what was assigned (ChatGPT-4 for students' own coursework versus traditional teacher-led instruction with no AI), the tool, the comparison arm, the between-subjects structure, and the arm counts, and p. 5 does say participants were 'randomly assigned', at the class level. But the paper calls its design quasi-experimental in the abstract and in Section 3.1, says it was chosen over strict randomisation, never gives the number of classes, and prints no baseline test, so design_class field_rct is not supported and criterion 1 stays unclear until the number of classes per arm is known.
